//: stylelint-config-standard supplies the correctness rules (unknown properties, duplicate selectors, deprecated values). Four of its stylistic opinions are turned off below because this repository deliberately does not follow them, so `npm run lint:css` reports only debt Phase 5 intends to clear and the flip from warnings to errors needs no disable comments. declaration-block-single-line-max-declarations and rule-empty-line-before: the application stylesheets write short rules on one line and group them without blank lines on purpose. no-descending-specificity: a cascade built on breakpoint overrides trips it by design, and reordering the file to satisfy it would move pixels for no benefit. media-feature-range-notation: it contradicts media-feature-name-allowed-list below, which permits only max-width, so satisfying either would fail the other. The breakpoint canon is the four max-width steps documented in docs/theming.md; min-width is allowed for one shape only -- the touch-tablet guard `(pointer: coarse) and (min-width: 761px)`, which max-width cannot express -- and is pinned to 761px, the exclusive complement of the 760px step, so it can never drift away from the canon it mirrors.

selector-class-pattern.message: Expected kebab-case or BEM in an application stylesheet, camelCase in a CSS module

overrides.//: The primitive tier is the one place a colour is allowed to be written down: `color-no-hex` and the rgb()/hsl() disallow-list exist to push every literal into app/styles/tokens-*.css, so firing them there asks the palette to point at itself. Without this exemption the rule Phase 5 flips to errors could never be satisfied, and the token files would carry the only warnings nobody may fix. font-family stays disallowed: --font-sans and --font-mono are custom properties, not font-family declarations, so the token files do not trip it and a real font-family literal in one of them would still be caught.
